maritime.title: NERAI Maritime Weekly
events: US-Iran Mutual Pause in Airstrikes Opens First Diplomatic Off-Ramp
Houthis Strike Saudi Tankers and Threaten Bab el-Mandeb Blockade, Opening Second Chokepoint Crisis
US Naval Blockade of Iran Tightens: 12 Ships Redirected, Two Tankers Boarded
Gulf Producers Race to Build Hormuz Bypass Infrastructure as Oil Touches $100
Ukraine Strikes Iranian Ship in Caspian Sea; Iran Warns of 'Unforeseen' Consequences
maritime.summary: The week was dominated by the simultaneous disruption of both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, as the active US-Iran conflict and a renewed Houthi blockade campaign against Saudi tankers compressed global oil shipping into its most constrained configuration in years. A US-Iran mutual pause in airstrikes announced on 27 July introduced the first diplomatic opening of the conflict, triggering a sharp oil-price correction, but the structural damage to tanker routing, freight rates, and shipper confidence remains acute. The dual-chokepoint crisis is now forcing lasting rerouting decisions and accelerating Gulf producers' investment in overland bypass infrastructure.

sanctions.title: NERAI Sanctions Weekly
events: US Lukoil License Expires; Bulgaria Scrambles on Refinery Asset Transfer
EU Sanctions Russian Energy Giant Inter RAO, Owner of 75% of Telasi
US Treasury Sanctions Muslim Brotherhood and Hamas Financial Networks
US Treasury Sanctions Iran Financial-Evasion Network
Houthis Declare Maritime Blockade of Saudi Arabia, Threatening Gulf Shipping
sanctions.summary: This week's sanctions landscape was shaped by five distinct pressure points: a US license expiry forcing an accelerated Lukoil asset divestiture in Bulgaria, a broad US Treasury action against Muslim Brotherhood and Hamas financial networks, a fresh EU energy-sector designation targeting Inter RAO, an Iran financial-evasion sanctions round, and a Houthi maritime blockade declaration against Saudi Arabia that is rattling Gulf shipping lanes. Taken together, the week signals continued aggressive use of US and EU unilateral economic tools across the Middle East, Eastern Europe and energy corridors, even as US-Iran indirect talks create a fragile pause in kinetic escalation.
